en: Sutta Nipāta 1.5 Cundasutta “I ask the Sage of abundant wisdom, who has reached the further shore of all phenomena.”
(Thus Cunda the smith’s son [addressed] the Buddha,
the Lord of Dhamma, free from craving;
the supreme among bipeds, the most excellent of charioteers.)
“How many ascetics are there in the world? Please tell me this.
“There are four ascetics; there is no fifth, Cunda,” said the Blessed One.
Being questioned as a witness,
I shall reveal to you those who are the conquerors of the path and the teachers of the path,
and him who lives by the path and him who defiles the path.
“Whom do the Buddhas call the Victor of the Path?
(Thus Cunda the smith’s son asked) How is the Proclaimer of the Path incomparable?”
"Tell me, when asked, how one lives by the path;
then reveal to me the defiler of the path.
"One who has crossed beyond doubt and is free from the arrow..."
Delighting in Nibbāna, free from craving,
the leader of the world including its devas—
such a one the Buddhas call a conqueror of the path.
Having known that which is supreme as supreme,
he who here proclaims and analyzes the Dhamma—
that unshakable sage who cuts through doubt— him [one should honor].
The second [type of person] they call a guide on the path for monks:
he who lives restrained and mindful upon the well-taught path of the Dhammapada.
Practicing blameless steps,
they call him the third bhikkhu who lives by the path;
having made a screen for those of good vows, he dwells.
One who is impetuous, a defiler of families, and shameless;
a deceiver, unrestrained, and a chatterer,
who walks in a counterfeit manner— he is a defiler of the path.
And the wise, learned noble disciple who has penetrated this as a householder, having understood that all [others] are not like this,
[realizes: "I am one who has transcended birth."
Having seen this, his faith does not falter.
For how could one who is corrupted make the uncorrupted equal to the pure by means of the impure?
The Cundasutta is the fifth.
